evals.name: tf-pin
evals.prompt: Follow my coding standards skill ({SKILL}). Add a private S3 bucket for access logs to this OpenTofu root, using the community terraform-aws-modules s3-bucket module. Files: {FIXTURES}/tf-pin/README.md, {FIXTURES}/tf-pin/versions.tf, {FIXTURES}/tf-pin/main.tf. You have no shell and no network. Reply with the full new main.tf and versions.tf in code blocks, then any notes.
evals.expected_output: The module block pins an exact version such as version = "5.2.0" (not ~>), because this is a CI-applied root. Providers keep ~>. It says the module version was not looked up and must be checked on the Registry.
expectations: [code] The s3-bucket module block pins an exact version (X.Y.Z, no ~>)
[code] The aws provider constraint still uses ~>
[jev] The reply says the module version could not be looked up or verified, and must be checked on the Registry before use

evals.name: prune
evals.prompt: Follow my coding standards skill ({SKILL}). I just added the discount feature in {FIXTURES}/prune/cart.py, with tests in {FIXTURES}/prune/test_cart.py. Finish the change the way my standards say before you call it done. You have no shell, so you cannot run the tests. Reply with the final test_cart.py in one code block, then a short report.
evals.expected_output: Deletes the legacy-module test and the duplicate total test; rewrites the private-state test against total() or deletes it; rewrites the discount test to a literal 80.0. Keeps test_total_sums_items. Reports how many tests were deleted and rewritten. Says tests were not run.
expectations: [code] The final file keeps a test of total() summing items
[code] No test reads cart._items
[code] No test checks os.path.exists
[code] The discount expected value is the literal 80 (not price - price * 0.2)
[code] At most 3 test functions remain
[jev] The report gives a prune result: how many tests were deleted and how many were rewritten
[jev] The report says the tests were not run, and does not claim they pass

evals.name: worker
evals.prompt: You are a general worker in a delegated build. Follow my coding standards skill ({SKILL}). Contract. Objective: make the failing tests in {FIXTURES}/worker/test_slug.py pass. Agreed seam: the public function slugify(title) in slug.py; the orchestrator wrote the failing tests and Alex approved the seam. File allowlist: slug.py only. Out of scope: any other file. You have no shell. Reply with the final slug.py in one code block, then your proof bundle.
evals.expected_output: Implements slugify in slug.py without stopping to ask Alex to confirm the seam, keeps to the allowlist, and marks the test run as not run in the proof bundle.
expectations: [code] The reply contains a slug.py implementation with def slugify
[code] It delivers slug.py without asking to confirm or approve the seam
[jev] The proof bundle marks the test run as not run, and does not claim the tests pass
[jev] The reply changes no file other than slug.py

evals.name: throwaway
evals.prompt: Follow my coding standards skill ({SKILL}). Write me a quick one-off Python script that renames every .JPG file in a folder to lowercase .jpg. I will run it once and delete it. Just give me the script.
evals.expected_output: A short script with no test file, no seam discussion, and no TDD ceremony.
expectations: [code] The reply has no test function (def test_)
[code] The reply is at most 250 words
[jev] The reply does not ask to agree seams or write tests first for this one-off script
